summary: Kickoff for onboarding Silverstone Health onto Redwood's hosted and dedicated options. Covered architecture, security requirements (SOC2/HIPAA concerns, SSO, KMS), success criteria, timeline, and next steps for provisioning a staging account and technical deep dive.
transcript:
Header: 2026-10-29 15:00 PT | Duration: ~53m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Emily Carter (Silverstone Head of Data), Dr. Alan Ruiz (CTO), Sofia Morales (Security Lead), Noah Kim (Platform), Priya Desai (Product)

Summary: quick intros, goals for first 90 days, security checklist, network/topology constraints, demo scheduling and next steps.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Ava with Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick round robin please.
[00:12] Emily Carter: Hi Emily here, head of data at Silverstone. excited to get started.
[00:18] Dr. Alan Ruiz: Alan Ruiz, CTO, we'll focus on infra and compliance side.
[00:24] Sofia Morales: Sofia, security lead - i'll be driving the questionnaire and compliance checklist.
[00:30] Noah Kim: Noah, platform engineer, i'll be working with ravi on network and deploys.
[00:36] Marcus Lee: Marcus from Redwood CSM, i'll be your day-to-day for onboarding.
[00:40] Ravi Patel: hi all, ravi se, i'll cover tech deep dive and benchmarks.

[03:00] Ava Chen: Goal for today - align on success criteria, timelines, who owns what, and get a plan to provision a staging test environment. hoping to scope a first-week smoke test and a 6-8 week pilot. any constraints?
[03:28] Emily Carter: timeline's important for us. we have an internal kickoff to execs mid-november, so ideally staging by early november and a small pilot by end of november.
[03:45] Dr. Alan Ruiz: we also need to validate latency and cost numbers vs our current infra. we're looking for 200ms p95 on 1k qps sort of expectations, but we'll see what model choices imply.

[06:10] Ravi Patel: ok good, from tech perspective we'll start with hosted api to get initial evals then propose dedicated for predictable throughput. can we talk about data residency and PII handling?
[06:24] Sofia Morales: yep, PII is a hard stop for some workloads. we need to know logs retention, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS support, and if you support customer-managed keys. also SSO/SAML and RBAC for console access.
[06:40] Ava Chen: absolutely - Redwood supports CMEK via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated. hosted has tenant separation and configurable retention; we can share our SOC2 docs and the security questionnaire. (slight pause) i'll attach the security pack after this call.

[09:50] Emily Carter: on the networking side, we run in AWS us-east-1 but have some services in GCP for analytics. we prefer private connectivity for the pilot, ideally VPC peering or private link.
[10:05] Noah Kim: yes we have strict egress rules; we need to understand IP ranges, egress ports, and any NAT gateway requirements.
[10:20] Ravi Patel: for Dedicated/Private we can do VPC peering or a private endpoint. i'll get the network checklist over. note - sometimes customers mix regions and we fallback to compatible model variants, but we'll document that tradeoff.

[13:15] Dr. Alan Ruiz: curious about model lifecycle  can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts? we run nightly batch jobs and realtime APIs.
[13:30] Marcus Lee: yep - rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback policies are supported in Redwood Console. we'll show you the rollout UI in the deep dive.

[16:05] Sofia Morales: SOC2 is fine, but do you handle HIPAA level attestations? we've got PHI in some flows.
[16:20] Ava Chen: Redwood has customers in healthcare and we have controls for HIPAA covered workflows  typically that implies Private deployment with CMEK and additional BAAs. i'll connect you with our compliance team for BAAs and a HIPAA-specific checklist.

[18:45] Emily Carter: on performance - what's the typical latency for smaller models vs larger ones, and how does batching/kv cache impact p95?
[19:00] Ravi Patel: typical hosted latencies vary  small opt-style models can be 80-120ms p50 and 150-250ms p95 depending on sequence length; larger dense models are higher. batching helps throughput but adds tail latency. we use KV cache and prefix caching to lower token costs for repeated prompts. note - sometimes the transcriber calls it KV "cash" so docs might have typos.

[22:10] Noah Kim: for benchmarking we want a reproducible harness. can you provide a spreadsheet of model perf and recommended quantization profiles?
[22:25] Ava Chen: yes, we'll share Redwood's model catalog performance sheet and suggested quantization and concurrency configs for your workload.

[25:30] Marcus Lee: Success criteria from our perspective  agreed staging up, sample traffic run with 95th latency targets documented, security signoff from Sofia, and a cost estimate. Emily, is that aligned?
[25:45] Emily Carter: yes that's good. add capacity planning for peak hours; we have spiky traffic.

[28:00] Dr. Alan Ruiz: what about costs  hosted per-token vs a reserved Dedicated commit? we need ballpark numbers to present to finance.
[28:15] Ava Chen: i'll send tiered pricing  hosted per-token, discounts for reserved committed monthly capacity, and an estimate model for hybrid where you use hosted for burst and dedicated for baseline.

[31:40] Sofia Morales: questions on audit logs and retention  we need immutable logs for three years for some workflows. can Redwood export audit logs to our SIEM?
[31:55] Ravi Patel: yes we can stream audit logs and provide long-term retention as an add-on; for Private deployments logs can be customer-managed and shipped to your S3 or SIEM.

[35:20] Marcus Lee: next steps recap  we'll provision a staging account, share security docs, and schedule the tech deep dive. i have notes to include a live benchmark session.
[35:40] Emily Carter: can we do a live bench where we replay a small subset of real traffic? we can obfuscate PHI prior to share.
[35:55] Ravi Patel: absolutely, a replay test helps validate caching and tokenization differences. we'll provide a test harness and samples.

[39:10] Ava Chen: any blockers on your side for the dates we discussed?
[39:18] Priya Desai: none, product is excited. execs need the cost estimate but otherwise clear.

[42:00] Sofia Morales: small thing - SSO needs to be SAML-based and we use Okta. is that supported?
[42:10] Marcus Lee: yes Okta SAML SSO supported. we'll include setup steps and metadata exchange doc.

[45:30] Dr. Alan Ruiz: who will be our primary technical contact at Redwood for the deep dive?
[45:38] Ravi Patel: that'll be me; i'll work with Noah for network and Marcus for onboarding flows.

[48:00] Ava Chen: great, recap and owners: Ava send onboarding guide + security pack; Marcus schedule deep dive; Ravi provide network checklist and perf catalog; Silverstone to provide network diagram and security answers.

[50:15] Emily Carter: thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[50:20] Ava Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links.

Action Items (verbatim in transcript): Ava to attach SOC2 and security pack; Marcus to schedule deep dive; Ravi to provision staging test plan and perf sheet; Silverstone to return questionnaire.

Links referenced: onboarding-guide.redwood/docs (link), redwood-security-pack.pdf (link), model-performance-catalog.xlsx (link), network-checklist.md (link).

End of call.
